task_summary: Parallelize a sequential TF-IDF search engine using Python multiprocessing, implementing parallel index building and parallel batch query search with correctness guarantees and performance targets.
decomposition_rationale: The task has two distinct parallelization targets (index building and batch search) that share common multiprocessing patterns but have fundamentally different computational structures. Index building is a MapReduce problem (chunk, compute local TF/DF, merge), while batch search requires distributing a large read-only index to workers via the initializer pattern. A third concern is ensuring result determinism. These map cleanly to 3 skills.

skills.name: evo-parallel-index-building
skills.description: Provides utilities for parallelizing TF-IDF inverted index construction using a MapReduce approach: chunking documents, computing local TF and DF in worker processes, merging partial results, and finalizing TF-IDF scores with global DF.
skills.responsibility: Document chunking, parallel map phase for local TF/DF computation, merging partial inverted indices and document frequencies using Counter.update() and defaultdict.extend(), and finalizing TF-IDF scores from raw counts.
dr_sections: 10. Efficient Patterns for Merging Partial Results
1.4 Code Example: Chunking and Mapping Documents

skills.name: evo-parallel-batch-search
skills.description: Provides utilities for parallelizing batch query search over a pre-built TF-IDF index, using the worker initializer pattern to efficiently share the read-only index across worker processes without repeated pickling.
skills.responsibility: Worker initializer setup for sharing large index data, parallel query dispatch using ProcessPoolExecutor or multiprocessing.Pool with initializer/initargs, per-query search logic in workers, and result collection.
dr_sections: 3.1 Passing the Index: Approaches and Trade-offs

skills.name: evo-parallel-determinism
skills.description: Provides patterns and utilities to ensure parallel TF-IDF results are identical to the sequential baseline, addressing floating-point ordering, dictionary/set ordering, tie-breaking, and pickling compatibility.
skills.responsibility: Deterministic score accumulation order, tie-breaking in result sorting, ensuring NamedTuples/dataclasses are module-level picklable, handling spawn vs fork context selection, and __name__ guards.
dr_sections: 5. Ensuring Identical Results to Sequential Version
8. NamedTuple and Dataclass Patterns for IPC
